technique_name: Wàng Yuè Píng Héng (Gazing at the Moon Balance)
deduction_content: Torso held 45° or more above horizontal level
Waist not twisted toward the rear in the direction of the supporting leg
Instep of the raised bent leg not extended flat

questions.question: What is the error code for Wàng Yuè Píng Héng (Gazing at the Moon Balance)?
What are the three main deduction points for Wàng Yuè Píng Héng?
questions.answer: Deductions are applied when: 1) Torso is held 45° or more above horizontal level, 2) Waist is not twisted toward the rear in the direction of the supporting leg, and 3) Instep of the raised bent leg is not extended flat.
choices: Deductions are applied when: 1) Toes of slapped foot not above shoulder level, 2) Slap missed and/or inaudible.

questions.question: What is the correct torso position for Wàng Yuè Píng Héng?
questions.answer: The torso should be held below 45° from the horizontal level.
choices: Deductions are applied when: 1) Straight sword and forearm or wrist are aligned, 2) No obvious vertical circle formed.

questions.question: How should the waist be positioned in a correct Wàng Yuè Píng Héng balance technique?
questions.answer: The waist should be twisted toward the rear in the direction of the supporting leg.
choices: A deduction is applied when the raised leg is held below horizontal level.

questions.question: What is the correct position for the raised leg in Wàng Yuè Píng Héng?
questions.answer: The instep of the raised bent leg should be extended flat with a clear inclination.
